items.text: The former deputy inspector of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters said that Israel's intelligence and security infiltration in the recent war goes beyond mobile phones, and surveillance cameras in streets, shops, and homes are also used to collect information and monitor individuals.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, criticized the consequences of the country's exit from the European Union, saying Brexit has created trade barriers for businesses. He is scheduled to sign agreements to expand cooperation at meetings in London and Brussels.
According to a video received by Iran International, on Tuesday, 26 Aban, the people of Abdanan came out in large numbers to protest in the streets and tore down a banner belonging to the Basij.

On Monday, 25 Aban 1405, the death sentences of five prisoners were carried out in the prisons of Abadan, Arsanjan, Damavand, Ferdows, and Marand. These prisoners had been sentenced to death for charges of intentional murder and drug-related crimes. The identities of these individuals were reported as Siavash Hosseini, Hossein Manouchehri, Hamid Khodabakhsh, Esmail Pouramshel, and Yaghoub Heydarpour.

Despite claims of self-sufficiency in wheat production and allocation of hundreds of thousands of billions of tomans in subsidies, subsidized bread purchases have been limited in some cities in Iran. Officials talk about saving flour consumption, but people face rising bread prices and bakers complain about increased costs. Mehdi Beigi has examined the roots of the bread crisis in Iran in "Peyvast".

On Tuesday, 26 Aban, a group of citizens held a protest in front of the General Directorate of Prisons in Gilan. These citizens, holding photos of some prisoners under death sentence including Manouchehr Fallah, Peyman (Amin) Farahavar, Zahra Shahbaz Tabari, and Yaghoub Derakhshan, demanded a halt to executions in Iran.
Images of explosions in Qeshm have been released. Government sources have not yet accepted that it was an attack and wrote "The exact nature of the explosions is still unclear."
After a deadly bus accident in Abdanan, Ilam province, some people in this city held a protest march, chanting slogans against the Islamic Republic and in support of Prince Reza Pahlavi.

Amir Ghalenoei, head coach of Iran's football team, criticized the tight match schedule and poor condition of the grass field. He said Iran's team rested one day less than Iraq and did not have enough time to hold even one proper tactical training session. These remarks were made in an interview with Mohammad Taghavi, former national team and Esteghlal club footballer.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said if there is a threat from Iran, they will pay a price that no country has paid before. He added he hopes Iran does not do such a thing, but the US takes threats "very seriously" and "they must be crazy" to do so. Trump emphasized that for this reason Iran should not have nuclear weapons.
American forces targeted an Islamic Republic air defense missile launcher in the Nariman area of Qeshm Island. Reports indicate at least six attacks occurred in this area.

After CNN reported a possible plan by the Islamic Republic to attack Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon, Donald Trump warned Tehran that it would pay a heavy price if such an attack occurred. The Islamic Republic denied these accusations, and security measures have been increased to protect senior US government officials.

Ahmad Nafisi, the political, security, and social deputy of Hormozgan province, confirmed on Tuesday, 26 Aban, that the US army attacked points within the Qeshm Island area and said this attack did not cause damage to residential, commercial areas, or the island's infrastructure. Nafisi added that the situation on Qeshm Island is under control and all emergency, service, and executive agencies are on full alert.

Wayne Rooney, former England football star, revealed in the podcast "Life at the Midpoint" that during his peak days at Manchester United, he struggled with alcohol consumption, isolation, and suicidal thoughts. He said that during his best sporting days, he would lock himself at home and think about suicide. A warning was issued that if encountering people showing signs of depression or suicidal tendencies, one should seek help from a trusted doctor or relevant organizations.

Sadegh Khajesteh, head of the Social Emergency Department of Khuzestan Welfare, reported that 843 cases of child abuse were registered in social emergency calls in this province since the beginning of the current year. He also stated that several cases including suicidal thoughts and attempts and severe family disputes were reported in the calls.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, on Tuesday, 26 Aban, denied reports about Iran planning to use chemical weapons in Washington and building missile bases under dams. Araghchi called these reports "nonsense" and "Iraq war-style propaganda" and accused pro-Israel media of publishing them.
A Panama-flagged tanker named "Tara Gas" caught fire extensively following an attack north of the city of Khasab, Oman.

At least three fuel-smuggling vehicles overturned following military forces shooting in Saravan. It was reported that on the current day, after military forces fired at fuel-smuggling vehicles on the Gasht axis in Saravan county, at least three vehicles overturned. The physical condition of the occupants of these vehicles was reported as severe and critical.

Due to ongoing air pollution, 920 non-infectious cardiac and respiratory patients visited medical centers under the coverage of Jundishapur University of Medical Sciences in Ahvaz during the 24 hours ending on the morning of 26 Aban.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International on Tuesday, 25 Aban, showing the cutting of trees in the Farmanieh neighborhood of Tehran and said that when asked about the reason, they were told the municipality had ordered it.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International on Tuesday, 26 Aban, reporting that after a large gathering of people in Abdanan against the Islamic Republic, government agents attacked them and dispersed the crowd with aerial gunfire and tear gas.

Attacks by the US and Israel on Mehrabad Airport on 15 and 17 Esfand 1404 destroyed a significant part of the Islamic Republic's military transport and refueling fleet. Satellite images show at least three Ilyushin 76, seven Antonov 74, two Boeing 747 refuelers, and two Boeing 707 aircraft were destroyed. The two destroyed Boeing 747s were the only operational supertankers in the fleet.

According to a report received by Iran International, security forces of the Islamic Republic violently arrested Sepideh Gholian's father and her 17-year-old nephew on Tuesday, 25 Aban, during a raid on her family home in Dezful. Afterwards, Mehdi Gholian, her brother, was also arrested and transferred to Dezful prison. The agents stated that the five-year suspended sentence of Sepideh Gholian has been enforced, and until Sepideh surrenders herself, her father and nephew will not be released.
Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, met and talked with the Sultan of Oman during his trip to Muscat.
A contract worker at Fanavaran Petrochemical Company who was injured in an accident on Sunday, 24 Aban, died after 36 hours of hospitalization.

A prisoner sentenced to death in Karaj Central Prison was released from execution after obtaining the consent of the victim's family. This prisoner had been sentenced to death 12 years ago for murder during a family dispute.

Trump issued a sharp warning about Tehran's "dirty bomb" in Washington. It was also reported that people in Abdanan have returned to the streets. These news were released in the audio version of Titrawol with Niusha Saremi.

The executive secretary of the Workers' House in Saveh reported the layoff of more than 1,500 workers in the industrial units of this city since the start of the recent wartime conditions. The first vice president of the Supreme Nursing Council said that the average arrears of nurses in the country have reached about six months.

Lionel Scaloni, Argentina's coach, joked about Lionel Messi possibly joining the national team's coaching staff after Walter Samuel's departure, saying: "If he wants to come here, there is no problem." He also expressed Messi's desire to continue playing football even after 2030.

According to videos received by Iran International, a large crowd of people in Abdanan took to the streets today, chanting slogans against the Islamic Republic and in support of Prince Reza Pahlavi. Some citizens reported attacks by agents on this gathering, weakening of the internet, and hearing the sound of aerial gunfire in Abdanan. This protest gathering took place after the death of 13 oil company workers in the overturning of their bus.

Thirteen employees of the Dehloran Petro-Refinery died on their way back from work. After this accident, people in Abdanan took to the streets and, according to videos received by Iran International, chanted slogans against the government and in support of Pahlavi.

The Iranian national football team drew 1-1 with Iraq in a friendly match on Tuesday afternoon, 26 Aban 1405. Hussein Ali scored for Iraq in the 22nd second and Mohammad Amin Hezbavi scored for Iran in the 83rd minute. The match was held at Basra Stadium in Iraq and was the national team's second preparatory match during the last international break in 2026.

Arash Aramesh, a national security expert, referred to reports about a possible plan by the Islamic Republic to attack in the US and said Washington's response depends on the progress of this planning and the presence of evidence of deployment of personnel and equipment for its execution.

Contrary to Iran's international commitments under the Convention on the Rights of the Child and obligations related to the non-use of children in military affairs, 1880 students from Semnan province and the counties of Gachsaran, Galikesh, Sardasht, Sarpol-e Zahab, Mahabad, and Abbasabad were sent to operational areas in the south of the country.

Prince Reza Pahlavi warned in a virtual meeting with Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, that the Islamic Republic will strive at any cost to obtain nuclear weapons if it continues to exist and will not hesitate to start a "second and much larger Holocaust." He also said that 40,000 Iranians have sacrificed their lives to defeat the Islamic Republic and called for solidarity and support for the Iranian people. Isaac Herzog said the war is not with the Iranian people but with a regime that seeks Israel's destruction and called for a coalition to confront the Islamic Republic.

UN experts recently issued a statement about Iranian porters. According to them, since the beginning of 2026, at least 12 porters have been killed by border guards or the IRGC. Also, from January to August of the same year, 13 Baloch fuel carriers have died.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said on the program "Cheshmandaz" that the upcoming meeting of the leaders of the US, China, and Russia has raised concerns about a great powers' agreement on dividing spheres of influence. According to him, Ukrainian officials have also expressed concern about turning this meeting into a "second Yalta."
A baker sent a video to Iran International showing the rationed flour sent to his shop and said: "The flours are very low quality; the lowest quality flour."

The Cannes Festival condemned the issuance of a five-year and one-month prison sentence, asset confiscation, two years of travel ban, and two years of social media activity ban for Jafar Panahi, an Iranian filmmaker, and called for the removal of restrictions that prevent his travel, artistic activity, and freedom of expression. The festival emphasized that no artist should be imprisoned for their artistic activities or expression of beliefs and urged the global community to act to prevent his imprisonment.

According to an eyewitness, two waterspouts were seen on Monday, November 16, near Highway 101 and the Candlestick Point area over San Francisco Bay in California. The US National Weather Service issued a special marine warning for the south of the Bay Bridge and confirmed the sighting of a waterspout; this warning included winds over 34 knots and rough waves.

Alireza Mansourian, head coach of Al-Zawraa team in Iraq, said that the Iraqi Football Federation has asked for his help if there are changes in the national team. He added that if the current national team coach, Graham Arnold, insists on leaving, he might become the national team coach. Mansourian left Al-Talaba last week and took charge of Al-Zawraa.

Iraj Heydari, Saeed Abdollahi, and Behnam Moradi were arrested following protests in Abdanan. These protests were held in response to the death of 13 people in a bus overturn accident involving employees of the Dehloran Petro-Refinery.

Iran International obtained exclusive information about the identities of members of a network of Thai clerics residing in Iran who were planning to attack the Israeli embassy in Bangkok. They had come to study at the Al-Mustafa community center in Qom and were recruited by the Quds Force of the IRGC and Hezbollah's Unit 910.

Harana's investigation into the status of detainees from the December 1404 protests in Yazd prison indicates heavy prison sentences, ongoing judicial uncertainty, and extensive restrictions on prisoner conditions. Among 28 prisoners, 15 have been sentenced to 3 to 21 years in prison, and 13 remain in judicial limbo. Long-term visitation bans, pressure on families, and overcrowding in the isolation ward are also reported.

In the audio version of Cheshmandaz, it was reported that in an unprecedented meeting of the leaders of the US, China, and Russia, the issue of determining the fate of the Iranian government was discussed.

Prince Reza Pahlavi supported the protesters in Abdanan in a video message following the death of 13 workers in a bus overturn. He said the repression and crimes of the Islamic Republic have not broken the determination and will of the people and expressed pride in the people of Abdanan. He also expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and ended his message with the phrase "Light triumphs over darkness."

Gianni Infantino, FIFA president, is seeking a fourth term despite widespread criticism of the canceled private investment plan for World Cup commercial rights. The deadline for candidate nominations is Wednesday, November 18, 2026, and the election will be held on March 18, 2027, in Rabat, Morocco. The football confederations of Africa, South America, and Asia continue to support Infantino.

Prince Reza Pahlavi said in a message to the people of Abdanan that their "brave roar" showed that the "repression and crimes of the Islamic Republic" could not break their determination and will. He expressed pride in the people of Abdanan, sympathized with the bereaved families of the deceased workers and the people of the city, and added: "Light triumphs over darkness."

Press TV reported on Tuesday, 26 Aban, quoting the Navy of the Islamic Republic Army that the fourth oil tanker in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz caught fire due to hitting a naval mine. The Navy stated that the tanker had turned off its tracking system while passing through the area. No further details about the identity of the tanker or the extent of the damage have been released so far.

Human rights organizations Hana and Kordpa reported that at least six people, including a 15-year-old teenager, were arrested on Tuesday, 26 Aban [Gregorian: 2026-11-17] during protests in Abdanan. The detainees were identified as Iraj Heydari, Saeed Abdollahi, Sina Darvishi, Asghar Akbari, Mohsen Bavir, and Behnam Moradi. Kordpa reported the presence of special unit forces, severe internet disruption, and reports of tear gas and pellet guns fired at protesters.

Ahmad Alavi, an economist, referred to the reduction of fuel quotas in 11 border provinces and long gasoline lines, saying the Islamic Republic is gradually reducing quotas to push consumers to buy fuel at higher prices. He said limiting access to fuel reduces economic activities and leads to recession and unemployment. Alavi attributed the gasoline shortage to insufficient investment, refinery inefficiency, and aging transportation fleet, and said the government tries to blame smugglers for its inability to supply fuel.

Amir Ghalenoei, the national team coach, said after the draw with Iraq that they have started the path of youth development and will continue it. He asked the federation officials to arrange matches with big teams and was satisfied with the young players. Ghalenoei added that Iraq is a strong team but his team made nearly 600 passes and had 60% possession and managed to do great work with the younger players.

Ebrahim Roshandel, a former diplomat and member of the U.S. Homeland Security counterterrorism committee, said that the role of the military in decision-making in the Islamic Republic has become more prominent and the space for political initiative has been limited.

AS newspaper reported that Silvia Toya Vinyes, a 46-year-old Spanish fitness specialist, will probably join Manchester United alongside Mauricio Pochettino. Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of Manchester United from Wednesday, 27 Aban, and it is expected that his coaching staff from the US national team, including Silvia Toya, will accompany him. The club has not yet separately confirmed the appointment of this Spanish specialist.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said the Abdanan protests showed that threats from security and judicial officials have not prevented people from returning to the streets. He added that the repeated chants of "Long live the Shah" and support for Prince Reza Pahlavi in these protests invalidate claims about his declining popularity.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, called his speech at a webinar hosted by the Chaim Herzog Center for Middle East Studies and Diplomacy at Ben-Gurion University alongside Prince Reza Pahlavi a "great honor." He said this dialogue is another chapter in the longstanding friendship between the people of Iran and the Jews. Herzog also described the Iranian regime as an existential threat to Israel, the Middle East, Europe, and the world, stating that it brutally suppresses its people and spreads terrorism.

The Kuwaiti army announced early Wednesday that the country's air defense systems are countering hostile drone attacks. As of the time of this report, the Kuwaiti army has not provided further details.

Thirteen workers did not return home after their shift ended. The overturning of the Petrorefining employees' bus in Dehloran caused grief for families and led the people of Abdanan to protest in the streets. Kambiz Hosseini addresses this issue in the program.
A report about the return of street protests in Abdanan has been presented.

Matan Kahana, a member of the Yesh Atid party, was elected as the Speaker of the Knesset after six hours of parliamentary debate and opposition from Netanyahu's coalition. The Likud party called this election "a disgrace for all time" and said the Speaker was appointed unilaterally with the votes of supporters of terrorism. Likud also stated that Eisenkot, Bennett, and Lieberman chose supporters of terrorism over national unity, and history will remember this action.

Gila Gamliel, Israel's Minister of Technology, said in a webinar with Prince Reza Pahlavi that she stands with the people of Iran and Reza Pahlavi in the struggle for freedom. She also stated that the sustainable solution is replacing the Islamic regime with a democratic government, calling this fight for the people of Iran, their dignity, and their future.

Amir Giti, a reporter for Iran International, referred to a Reuters report about the deadlock in negotiations and said no clear information has been released by either side about the progress of talks. He added that officials of the Islamic Republic deny conducting negotiations. Also, Donald Trump described the continuation of the current situation and economic pressure as a way to reach the economic collapse of the Islamic Republic, and Scott Bassett emphasized the intensification of the economic crisis.

The Ministry of Interior of Bahrain issued a warning asking citizens and residents to maintain calm for public safety, go to the nearest safe place, and follow news through official channels. Meanwhile, Al Arabiya reported the sounding of sirens in Bahrain.

Forough Kenani, a sociology researcher and women's rights activist, said that anti-government slogans and support for Prince Reza Pahlavi at the Abdanan protest indicate that the repression in Dey has not eliminated the political demands of the people. She added that the protest following the overturning of a bus carrying workers has gone beyond demands for changing local officials and targeted the entire Islamic Republic. Kenani called on Iranians abroad to repost videos of the protests and attract the attention of political representatives in their countries of residence.

Roghayeh Rezaei, a journalist and member of IranWire editorial team, said the Abdanan protests following the overturning of a bus carrying workers should be examined in the context of years of deprivation and neglect of road safety and urban infrastructure. She added that poverty, livelihood instability, and loss of hope for the future have turned parts of society into a force for change. Each protest can create conditions for other groups to join and for the protests to expand.

Vladimir Putin, President of Russia, arrived in Shenzhen, Guangdong province in southern China early Wednesday to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. The summit will be held on Wednesday and Thursday. Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau and a member of the Secretariat of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, welcomed Putin at the airport.

Turkish police entered the building of one of the most watched government-critical TV networks in Istanbul early Tuesday and transferred its management to a government-appointed trustee by court order. This operation took place only one month after a similar action against another TV network and has increased opposition parties' concerns about media freedom.

Bahrain's Ministry of Interior, coinciding with the sounding of warning sirens again in the country, urged citizens and residents to remain calm, go to the nearest safe place, and follow news through official channels. Earlier, warning sirens had sounded in Bahrain in the early hours of Wednesday morning.

The Ministry of Defense of Bahrain stated that the Islamic Republic continues its "hostile and organized" approach with its "criminal attacks" against Bahrain. The ministry also emphasized that the country's air defense systems, with "firm will and high combat readiness," repelled several "treacherous air attacks" by the Iranian government early Wednesday.

The Public Relations of the Islamic Republic Army announced that early Wednesday, the Patriot air defense systems and the drone and missile launch platforms of the US Army at Ali Al-Salem base in Kuwait were targeted with destructive drones. Earlier, the Kuwaiti army had reported that its air defense countered "hostile drone attacks."

Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced three detainees of the nationwide protests of Dey 1404 to death on charges of operational action for Israel. Nazli Sedghi, a lawyer, explains the legal and political weaknesses of this case in terms of the trial process and the need for approval.

The Prime Minister of Iraq ordered the halt of tankers carrying oil and oil products to combat fuel smuggling. The government spokesperson announced the entry of armed forces into Jurf al-Sakhar and the end of the deadline for the withdrawal of Kata'ib Hezbollah.

The annual APEC senior officials meeting began in Shenzhen, China, with over two thousand representatives from 21 member countries. Development of artificial intelligence and regional economic cooperation are main topics of this meeting. Simultaneously, Vladimir Putin arrived in China to attend the summit.

Canada and China have agreed to lift tariffs on some Canadian food and seafood products. This agreement was finalized during a meeting between Mark Carney, Prime Minister of Canada, and Xi Jinping, President of China, on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

Shahram Kholdi, a researcher of Middle Eastern history and international relations, said the Iranian national uprising remains one of the main variables in regional developments. He added that domestic, regional, and international developments indicate the world is approaching a consensus on determining the fate of the Islamic Republic.

Pope Leo XIV thanked the people of Peru for their welcome at the end of the Mass ceremony in Lima and said he came to deliver the message of Christ to this country but leaves with a memory of the people's faith and devotion.

Sadegh Beigdeli, a lawyer and political activist, said the Islamic Republic neither has the deterrence capability against the US nor is willing to surrender. He emphasized that the US will not agree to a deal without stopping the Islamic Republic's nuclear program and eliminating the possibility of this regime obtaining nuclear weapons. Beigdeli also said that a resolution against the Islamic Republic's attacks could serve as a basis for legal pursuit and compensation claims by the Gulf countries.

Gholamhossein Mohseni Eje'i, head of the judiciary of the Islamic Republic, stated that the armed forces are developing and updating their equipment and have equipment they did not have during the 40-day war. He said the armed forces have not retreated against the enemy and will not do so. Eje'i also announced that Donald Trump intends to attack the Islamic Republic again.

Morteza Mahmoudi, Tehran's parliamentary representative, said that Qatar plays in the puzzle of US policies by sending a signal of calm to the global market through diplomacy and tries to show a positive negotiation atmosphere. He added that continued uncertainty in the Strait of Hormuz has imposed heavy costs on the global economy. Mahmoudi said that the system's decision-makers are fully aware of Qatar's dual game and will not allow these diplomatic moves to become a tool for psychological market management.

The UAE news agency reported that one of the ships of ADNOC Shipping was attacked on the evening of Tuesday, 26 Aban, while passing through the Strait of Hormuz. In this attack, 11 crew members were injured and one person is missing. Search and rescue operations to find the missing person are ongoing.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International and wrote that a sand and gravel factory near Fardis started burning mazut this year, and its activity has affected the air quality in the area.

Amir Hatami, the commander-in-chief of the Islamic Republic Army, announced on Wednesday, 27 Aban, that the readiness of the military and armed forces "is improving moment by moment." He said the enemy is preparing its forces, but the army and armed forces are monitoring their movements. Hatami added that the armed forces' response to the enemy's mistake "will be more crushing" and warned that if anyone casts a hostile glance at Iran, it will serve as a lesson for all.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei, the deputy speaker of the parliament, said in the session on 27 Aban that some countries are helping the US and the Islamic Republic is responding. He warned that if a war occurs in the region, some kings will be trampled. Hajibabaei also said the US is unable to design a fake victory and Trump is confused in the US-Israel duality.

The Disciplinary Committee of the Football Federation rejected Tractor Club's complaint against Esteghlal regarding the use of three "unauthorized" players. The committee stated that Tractor did not provide sufficient documents to prove its claims and issued a verdict of acquittal. Also, in the case of Esteghlal's complaint against the assistant referee of the match against Esteghlal Khuzestan, a suspension of proceedings was issued.

Ali Shirazi, a member of the Iran International editorial team, said the protests of the people of Abdanan following the death of 13 people in a bus accident showed that the demands of the people since Dey 1404 remain intact and repression has not silenced the protesters. He added that the return of Prince Reza Pahlavi and the overthrow of the Islamic Republic remain among the main demands of the protesters, and the support of citizens in other cities for the people of Abdanan also indicates the spread of solidarity with these protests.

Rouhollah Rahimpour said there is no independent public evidence yet about the Islamic Republic planning terrorist attacks with a dirty bomb or chemical weapons in Washington, but the threat should be taken seriously. He added that if a connection between such operations and the Islamic Republic's command structure is proven, Washington might escalate its response from intelligence and cyber operations to extensive military attacks. Rahimpour described such an action as a costly miscalculation for Tehran and likely to create a broader international consensus against the Islamic Republic.
Swedish police say Rawa Majid, the leader of the Foxtrot criminal network, still plays a role in the network's criminal activities, and Swedish media have reported that he is likely in Iran.

Isaac Herzog, President of Israel, and Prince Reza Pahlavi held a virtual meeting discussing the future of Iran and the prospects for Tehran-Tel Aviv relations after the Islamic Republic. Herzog expressed hope that Prince Reza Pahlavi would return to Iran after the fall of the Islamic Republic and that peaceful relations between the two countries would be established. Prince Reza Pahlavi warned about the nuclear threats of the Islamic Republic and the danger of this regime obtaining nuclear weapons.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said during a trip to Qazvin province that stopping production and causing unemployment is exactly what enemies seek. He added that fuel and energy for industries should be the last option during restrictions to prevent halting production. Pezeshkian emphasized that his priority is to never allow the production cycle to stop.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International stating that the price of a box of 2 mg clonazepam has risen from 70,000 tomans before the New Year and 220,000 tomans 40 days ago to 472,000 tomans now. He criticized this price increase, saying: "I don't know what to do about the mullahs."

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, arrived in Shenzhen, China today, Wednesday, 27 Aban, after traveling to the Philippines. Xi Jinping, the President of China, personally welcomed Trump.

Messages received by Iran International indicate the continuation of a military and security atmosphere in Abdanan. At the same time, citizens from various parts of Iran have sent messages to Iran International's media contacts expressing their support for the protesters in Abdanan.

Xi Jinping, President of China, at the start of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, called for broader global cooperation in artificial intelligence and free trade. He also emphasized removing barriers to trade and investment and said China will advance deep reforms by reducing tariffs and opening more production and service sectors to foreign companies.
A video sent to Iran International shows a night patrol by police in the city of Lushan, a part of Rudbar county in the south of Gilan province.

Ghasem Qureshi, deputy head of the Basij Organization, said on Wednesday, 27 Aban, that by order of Mojtaba Khamenei, leader of the Islamic Republic, increasing missile range to counter new threats is on the armed forces' agenda. Qureshi added that missile and aerospace forces will strive with full capacity to realize this strategy. He also said that given the US withdrawal from the region, it is necessary to increase the range and retaliatory capability of the armed forces.

A video released on social media shows that Alireza Raeisi's family mourned at the grave of this unknown martyr in the deserts of Anarak. Alireza was arrested on 29 Dey and then sentenced to death on charges of "enmity against God." The sentence of this 21-year-old protester was carried out on 13 Mehr, and his body was buried without the family's knowledge on the edge of the desert plain in Isfahan province.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that in less than 9 months, about 45 attacks have been carried out against Kuwait, 30 of which targeted the Ali Al-Salem airbase. He linked Kuwait's warning about the dangerous escalation of tensions to the country's historical experience of Saddam Hussein's attacks and added that the Islamic Republic's assumption that it can continue its attacks without serious consequences does not align with historical experiences.

Jean-Noël Barrot, France's foreign minister, announced that France has sanctioned the perpetrators of the repression of the Iranian people and that a new sanctions package targets institutions responsible for the repression, especially the judiciary of the Islamic Republic. He added that those killed in the January protests in Iran last year included children, women, and men. Barrot also said that the US and Israel's war against the Islamic Republic and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz should not cause the repression of the Iranian people to be forgotten, and emphasized that they will not allow the Iranian government's crimes against its people to go unpunished.

Jean-Noël Barrot, French Foreign Minister, emphasized Paris's support for human rights defenders in Iran and said France has imposed sanctions on individuals and entities involved in suppressing the Iranian people and is considering new sanctions. He also referred to widespread human rights violations during the January 2026 protests and the Woman, Life, Freedom movement, stressing that France still demands the IRGC be listed as a terrorist organization by the European Union.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, said in the French parliament that the Islamic Republic did not stop executions even during the war. She added that at least 39 people were executed in connection with the December protests, with at least five executed publicly. Sato also said that Iranian authorities used the war to divert attention from human rights violations and repression of protesters, and pressure on families of those killed in the protests has continued.

Jean-Noël Barrot, the French Foreign Minister, called on Wednesday, 27 Aban, for the adoption of a resolution at the UN General Assembly regarding the human rights situation in Iran. He said that crimes committed against the Iranian people should be declared crimes against humanity. Barrot also emphasized France's support for the Iranian people's struggle for freedom.
A video sent to Iran International shows a protesting citizen writing the slogan "Long live the Shah" on a street wall in the city of Estahban, Fars province.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, said in the French parliament that detainees are usually forced to confess under pressure a few days after arrest and without access to a lawyer. She referred to threats and arrests of lawyers and the lack of an independent mechanism to hold perpetrators of human rights violations accountable. Sato emphasized that impunity is a common theme in recent UN reports on Iran.

Mai Sato, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran, spoke in the French National Assembly about human rights violations and the suppression of protests in Iran. Jean-Noël Barrot, the French foreign minister, also announced pursuing measures including sanctions against those ordering the crackdown.

Rafael Grossi, Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency, stated that until the Islamic Republic provides information about its declared nuclear materials and facilities and allows on-site verification, the agency cannot confirm that nuclear materials have not been diverted from peaceful activities. Grossi said the agency has received no information nor access to facilities except for the Bushehr nuclear power plant. He added that the agency has lost the ability to monitor declared uranium inventories, including uranium enriched up to 60 percent, for nearly 18 months and cannot report on Iran's compliance with UN Security Council resolutions.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the Trump administration hopes to force the Islamic Republic to surrender or collapse through continued economic blockade and limited military clashes. He predicts that the Iranian government will rapidly escalate tensions in the region to break these pressures.

Real Madrid announced that the contract of Arda Güler, the Turkish midfielder, has been extended until June 30, 2032. Güler, who joined the team at age 18, has played 126 games and won five trophies. He has also played 38 times for the Turkish national team and received the best emerging player award of the UEFA Champions League for the 2025–2026 season.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International and said that every morning long queues of cars and motorcycles form at the gas station in the city of Ahel, Fars province. According to him, the formation of such queues in this small city is unprecedented.

Raha Bahraini, a researcher at Amnesty International, referred to the killing of protesters in the protests of Dey 1404 and emphasized the necessity of ending the immunity of perpetrators of crimes against humanity. She said many commanders and officials involved in the crackdown have not only not been punished but still hold senior positions, and some have even been promoted. Bahraini stressed that documenting these crimes is not enough and there must be legal and international consequences for those responsible.

Today, a group of dredging workers of Mahshahr and Bandar Imam water and wastewater company held a protest for the second time this week in front of Mahshahr governor's office. These workers are protesting against their wage and insurance arrears over the past four months. They say that after the contractor company left the municipality, their employment status has been uncertain and they have been without work and income since last month.

The head of Shiraz University of Medical Sciences reported that about 800 people lost their lives in road accidents in Fars province during the first six months of this year. Seyed Basir Hashemi said nearly 10,000 people were injured in accidents. He pointed to the role of environmental factors, vehicle technical issues, and human error in the occurrence of accidents.

Rafael Grossi, Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency, said the agency has not inspected Iran's nuclear facilities for over a year and has lost the ability to verify the status of nuclear materials and enriched uranium stocks. He emphasized that Tehran must allow inspections as a member of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

The four-semester temporary suspension from studies of Pejman Nasiri, a seventh-term undergraduate student in textile design and former secretary of the student council at Iran University of Art, was confirmed by the university's appeals committee.

Rafael Grossi, Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency, said on Wednesday, 27 Aban, at a Board of Governors press conference in Vienna that the issue of lack of access to Iran's uranium reserves must be resolved immediately and that it cannot be said where Iran's nuclear materials are or what has happened to them. He added that a way must be found to resume inspections and emphasized that Iran is a member of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and inspections of its nuclear facilities must be possible. Grossi also said regarding the possibility of Iran leaving the treaty that the decision is Iran's sovereign right but he does not consider leaving a wise decision.

The Iran Human Rights Documentation Center reported that Omid Janami, a 28-year-old bodybuilding athlete and detainee of the January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to death. His case is at the appeal stage in the Supreme Court. Janami was held in solitary confinement for 70 days and subjected to physical and psychological torture.

Payam Akhavan, a law professor and former prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, said that holding the France meeting with the country's foreign minister, members of the National Assembly, and the UN special rapporteur shows the importance of the crimes against humanity case in the Islamic Republic. He pointed to obstacles to referring the case to the International Criminal Court, including possible opposition from Russia and China and the US stance, and emphasized that a mechanism should be established in the UN General Assembly to address these crimes.

Yesterday, a group of employees of the Tehran Regional Electricity Company held a protest demanding the change of their employment status from employee to worker. The protesters had also held a protest on this issue in Khordad of this year.

According to information received by Iran International, Samaneh Asghari, the sister of Sajad Asghari who was killed in the January 1404 protests, suffered a stroke in her sleep and died due to psychological pressure from her brother's death. Their father wrote on Instagram that Samaneh could not bear the absence of her brother. Sajad Asghari was killed by a gunshot during the protests in Fardis, Karaj on January 9, 2027, and his family found his body with tied hands in a medical center after searching for him.

A group of Iranians residing in the Netherlands gathered on 26 Aban in front of the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs. One participant said the purpose of this gathering was to convey the voice of the Iranian people and protest what they called "the continued appeasement of the Dutch government towards the Islamic Republic." Participants chanted slogans such as "Long live Iran" and "Long live the Shah."

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh, Esteghlal's head coach, did not participate in Wednesday's training after protesting the lack of a suitable grass field and necessary team facilities. He has been waiting for the club managers' response to his requests for improving training conditions in recent days. In his absence, his assistants took charge of the training session.

Mohammadmahdi Toghiani, a political prisoner, is serving his 21-year sentence in Dastgerd prison in Isfahan. Amirhossein Toghiani, his son, has been held in legal limbo in Dastgerd prison for over 9 months, and no trial has yet been held for his charges. Mohammadmahdi Toghiani is accused of acting against national security and forming a group to overthrow, while Amirhossein faces charges of moharebeh.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of the Iran International editorial team, reacted to Masoud Pezeshkian's remarks about the role of the US in production stagnation and rising unemployment, saying the Islamic Republic avoids accountability for the consequences of its policies by attributing the country's crises to the enemy. He considered Pezeshkian's statements as an admission of a deep divide between the people and the government.

Amir Ghalenoei, the national team coach, after returning from Basra and a draw against Iraq in the FIFA date, said that if young players experience difficult conditions, they can build a good generation. He added that in the game against Iraq, they conceded a goal in the first minute but returned to the game and statistically had one of the best conditions.

A video received by Iran International shows that on Tuesday, 26 Aban, as part of the campaign "No to execution, no to the Islamic Republic," a group of Iranians held a protest in front of the British Prime Minister's office in London, chanting slogans such as "Long live Iran" and "Long live the Shah."

Alireza Beiranvand, goalkeeper of Tractor and one of the three final nominees for the Asian Footballer of the Year award, criticized the ban on Iranian representatives from hosting rights in the AFC Champions League and expressed hope that after 22 years this award would return to Iranian football. He said that the presence of Iranian fans can bring special enthusiasm and prestige to the league, and the lack of hosting has made conditions difficult for Iranian teams. Beiranvand also expressed happiness about being nominated again after seven years and said he has tried to perform well in every team he has played for.

Donald Trump, President of the United States, attended the official leaders' photo session alongside Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping on Wednesday, 27 Aban, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in Shenzhen, China. Trump had earlier entered the official dinner ceremony of the summit, welcomed by Xi Jinping and his wife. Upon arrival, he paid attention to the classical orchestra playing the patriotic anthem "America the Beautiful" and acknowledged the musicians with a gesture.

The number of detainees in Khash has reached three. Including Hamzeh Suri-Zahi and Mohammad Karim Suri-Zahi, the number of citizens detained by military and security forces in the Towhidabad Poshtkuh neighborhood of Khash has increased to three. The earlier detention of Rahman Suri-Zahi had been reported.
